rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without four witnesses, God's law counts the accusers as liars; Muslims therefore had no basis to believe their accusation.
rows.anchor: if they have failed to produce four witnesses, then according to the law of God, it is these people who are liars

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse repeats the admonition of 24:10: people must heed God's mercy lest they again become entangled in similar mischief.
rows.anchor: similar admonition to Muslims as the one sounded in verse 10 earlier

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole society is addressed although few were responsible, because this contagious misconduct could engulf everyone.
rows.anchor: This is because this ailment is contagious.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting information must be an intellectual process rather than hearsay; only information grounded in sound knowledge merits transmission.
rows.anchor: Accepting a statement must be an intellectual process not hearsay. Only that information is worthy of transmission which is based on sound knowledge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who replace thought with their tongues and repeat unverified reports join Satan's mischief and lure others into it.
rows.anchor: If a person refuses to use his intellect and only uses the services of his tongue, he will communicate everything he hears without confirming it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here subḥānaka means “God forbid”; Muslims should have disclaimed any authority to repeat an unfounded accusation against a believing woman, especially ʿĀʾishah.
rows.anchor: The implication is that when a certain piece of information which had no proof came into the knowledge of the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper response was to deny any right to state an unfounded claim maligning a believing woman and call it blatant slander.
rows.anchor: they have no authority to state something that is unfounded that maligns a believing woman; it is blatant slander

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses yield important principles for assessing reports, which scholars should consider.
rows.anchor: The principles that can be derived from these verses regarding the acceptance of a narrative are very important.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word waʿẓ itself conveys rebuke and prohibition, so it needs no additional negative particle.
rows.anchor: The meaning of rebuke and prohibition is found in the word وَﻋْﻆٌ .For this reason a particle of negation after it is not needed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses continue the warnings of the three preceding verses; God's directives in the sūrah protect people from His wrath.
rows.anchor: These verses also form a warning, the way the three earlier ones do.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abstaining from the unbecoming behavior is a requirement of faith; persistence would make the claim to faith baseless.
rows.anchor: abstaining from such an unbecoming attitude is a requisite of faith. If they do not desist from them, it would mean that their claim to faith is baseless.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God explains His directives and is wise, people must follow them and recognize their blessing rather than claim greater wisdom.
rows.anchor: since God is fully explaining His directives, the responsibility of following these rests on people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refers to the hypocrites who instigated the propaganda.
rows.anchor: This verse refers to the hypocrites who had instigated this propaganda.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews resented Muslims' moral reform: the changed purity made their own degradation more conspicuous and drove them to seek revenge.
rows.anchor: When they observed that this filth was being transformed into a purity that was enviable, they found themselves in a quandary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews used their dependent hypocrites to spread vice and targeted the Prophet's wives, hoping to damage Muslims' moral standing; God prevented the plot.
rows.anchor: To execute this plan, they employed the services of the hypocrites since they were under their influence and in fact had been nurtured by them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing reminder that God knows while people do not warns Muslims being drawn into the hypocrites' mischief without seeing their hidden enemies' plans.
rows.anchor: a warning to those Muslims who were being lured by this mischief of the hypocrites because they were not fully aware

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 20 repeats verse 10 but substitutes the divine attributes tawwāb and raḥīm with raʾūf and raḥīm.
rows.anchor: This very verse has occurred earlier too. See verse 10. The only difference is that there the attributes of God mentioned were

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer is omitted to intensify the warning; God's grace spared Muslims punishment for a grave error and gave them time to repent.
rows.anchor: it is purely because of the grace and mercy of God that He has not punished Muslims for this huge blunder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general warning reiterates the preceding directive against following Satan's path.
rows.anchor: This verse sounds a similar warning to the Muslims like the ones that have already been sounded before.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Passing on unverified information follows conjecture, which is to follow Satan; people must not transmit claims whose truth they cannot establish.
rows.anchor: What is without proof is mere conjecture and to follow conjecture is to follow Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting baseless accusations reveals self-righteous vanity: purification comes only by God's grace, so no one should accuse others without investigation.
rows.anchor: whoever attains purification does so merely because of God’s grace. If His graciousness is not present, none can be purified.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears and knows even people's hidden affairs, a reminder to those who give themselves excessive allowance.
rows.anchor: He hears and knows the most hidden things of people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should forgive and forgo the naive participants in the slander and keep helping them, since otherwise many might withdraw their support.
rows.anchor: people would refrain from financially helping and patronizing those who played any role in spreading this slander

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Misṭaḥ was Abu Bakr's needy relative and beneficiary; after learning he joined the slander, Abu Bakr grieved and swore to stop helping him.
rows.anchor: he too had a share in spreading this propaganda, Abū Bakr (rta) was naturally very sad and swore that he would never help him in future.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who want God to forgive their own mistakes should forgive others, reflecting God's forgiving and merciful qualities in their conduct.
rows.anchor: mistakes should forgive others too for their faults.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-given prosperity obliges the affluent to deal generously with others despite their own shortcomings.
rows.anchor: those who, in spite of their own shortcomings, have been granted prosperity in their livelihood by God are required by Him to deal generously with others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindred, the needy, and emigrants for God's cause must not lose help and support because they made a mistake.
rows.anchor: they should not be deprived of help and support merely because they have committed some mistake.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refusing to forgive others implies self-purification just as rumor-based condemnation does; both errors belong to the same religious category and are placed together.
rows.anchor: with regard to the philosophy of religion both these mistakes belong to the same category. Hence both are adjacently mentioned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥṣanāt denotes chaste upright women.
rows.anchor: means chaste upright women and

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāfilāt refers to innocent and virtuous women.
rows.anchor: refers to innocent and virtuous women. Though these words are used in a general sense

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording applies generally to decent upright Muslim women while subtly pointing especially to ʿĀʾishah as their leading example.
rows.anchor: they contain a subtle reference to ‘ Ā’ishah (rta). She was the most prominent person who could be referred to by these words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramy means both throwing an arrow and accusing or slandering someone.
rows.anchor: to throw an arrow, but it also means to accuse and to slander someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the word for slander evokes innocent women as targets of arrows while asleep.
rows.anchor: make such women a target of their arrows while they are sleeping.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slanderers of innocent women are cursed in this world and the next and succeed in neither.
rows.anchor: Such people who do this stand cursed both in this world and in the Hereafter. Neither will they succeed here nor there.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse was realized on earth when Islam became dominant and the hypocrites, including their leaders, were destroyed in Arabia.
rows.anchor: ultimately when Islam became dominant all of them including their leaders were totally destroyed in the land of Arabia.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the day of punishment, the accused will be unable to offer an excuse, and no external evidence will be needed to establish their crime.
rows.anchor: neither will they be able to present any excuse nor will any external evidence be needed to prove their crime.
